binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, implicitly quantified.
A and Ainv are arbitrary n-by-n real matrices, equivalently functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
c, uLow, and uHigh are arbitrary real numbers.
backwardError and forwardError are arbitrary sequences from the natural numbers to the real numbers.
hypotheses: Let K=||A||_F*||Ainv||_F and q=(c*uLow)*K. Then q<1.
For every natural number i, if c*uHigh < backwardError(i), then backwardError(i+1) <= q*backwardError(i).
For every natural number i, if (c*uHigh)*K < forwardError(i), then forwardError(i+1) <= q*forwardError(i).
conclusions: The backward threshold c*uHigh is nonnegative.
For every natural number i, q^i<=1.
For every natural number i, if c*uHigh < backwardError(j) for every natural number j<i, then backwardError(i) <= q^i*backwardError(0).
For every natural number i, if (c*uHigh)*K < forwardError(j) for every natural number j<i, then forwardError(i) <= q^i*forwardError(0).
mathematical_definitions: For a square real matrix X, ||X||_F denotes exactly the norm selected by Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing.
The backward threshold is tau_b=c*uHigh, and the forward threshold is tau_f=(c*uHigh)*K.
The contraction factor is q=(c*uLow)*K, and q^i is its ordinary i-th natural power, with q^0=1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, arbitrary n-by-n real matrices A and Ainv, nonnegative real parameters c, uLow, and uHigh, and arbitrary real-valued backward- and forward-error sequences, define K=||A||_F||Ainv||_F and q=c*uLow*K. Assume q<1. Assume that whenever the backward error at iteration i is strictly above c*uHigh, its next value is at most q times its current value, and whenever the forward error at iteration i is strictly above c*uHigh*K, its next value is at most q times its current value. Then both thresholds c*uHigh and c*uHigh*K are nonnegative. Moreover, for every natural number i, q^i<=1; if every backward error at an earlier index j<i is strictly above c*uHigh, then backwardError(i)<=q^i*backwardError(0); and if every forward error at an earlier index j<i is strictly above c*uHigh*K, then forwardError(i)<=q^i*forwardError(0).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n is unrestricted and may be zero.
Despite its name, Ainv is not assumed to be an inverse of A; no equation such as A*Ainv=I, nonsingularity condition, or relationship between the matrices is present.
The error sequences are arbitrary real-valued sequences and are not assumed nonnegative or connected to any matrix computation.
Each recurrence is conditional and constrains the next error only when the current error is strictly above its threshold.

Each geometric error bound is itself conditional on every earlier error being strictly above the relevant threshold. If even one earlier error is at or below the threshold, that implication has a false antecedent and supplies no bound at that index.
At i=0, each all-earlier-indices premise is vacuously true, but the resulting bound is only error(0)<=q^0*error(0)=error(0).
The proposition does not assert an unconditional global convergence result, a limit, a stopping index, or any behavior after an error reaches or falls below its threshold.
Nonnegativity of c, uLow, uHigh, and matrix norms implies 0<=q<1, but only q<1 appears as an explicit hypothesis; q^i<=1 is included explicitly in the conclusion.
ambiguities: The packet does not unfold Matrix.frobeniusSeminormedAddCommGroup, from which Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing inherits its norm. Thus the selected matrix norm is unambiguous as a Lean operation and is designated as the Frobenius-instance norm, but its entrywise formula and normalization cannot be independently recovered from the supplied bodies alone.
